text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Friday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Former Bank of Estonia president Siim Kallas was directly involved in preparing the transfer of $10 million of central bank's assets to a Swiss bank. Kallas said earlier the money belonged to the then state owned North-Estonian Bank and he had not been involved in the preparations.

- Baltic premiers met in Tallinn at the Baltic Council of Ministers session and signed documents on transit procedures, a Baltic customs union, inter-governmental data link, regional airspace control and co-operation in the European integration.
- The Tallinn Council approved the capital's budget for 1997, worth 2.1 billion kroons.

- Negotiations between politicians continue about the proposed vote of no confidence in Tiit Vaehi, following an apartment privatisation row, with no concrete results emerging. Mayor of Tallinn Robert Lepikson said he was not interested in standing for the prime minister's post.
- Estonia appointed new charges d'affaire to the Netherlands and Spain from mid-February.

- Russian ambassador Alexander Trofimov confirmed Russia's eagerness to have a border agreement with Estonia, but warned against adding unilateral declarations, which would make the ratification impossible.
- Enimex, a private-owned transport company, bought its third AN-72 transport aircraft from Russia furnished for VIP travel.
- Talleks formed a joint venture with the Danish Nordisk Motor to import Volkswagen cars to Estonia.
